meanings.note: Приятного аппетита!
+ genitive.
+ prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
predicative: очень вкусно = it's delicious
Вкусно готовить = to cook well.
polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

выходить.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить').

examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.
This is indeed an important question.
Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Ещё больше = even more.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Зал суда = courtroom. Common masculine noun meaning 'hall, large room; courtroom' in everyday Russian.
Regional/colloquial. Common masculine noun meaning 'hall, large room; courtroom' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Understood. And who is managing the dining room?
Let's find out the winner's name.

examples.text: Давайте узнаем имя нашего главного победителя!
examples.trans: Let's find out the name of our grand winner!

meanings.note: historical participant in the Crusades

examples.text: Крестоносцы готовили рыбу прямо на мечах.
examples.trans: The Crusaders prepared fish right on their swords.

examples.text: История о крестоносцах спасла ресторан от скандала.
examples.trans: The story about Crusaders saved the restaurant from scandal.

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: medieval hand-to-hand bladed weapon

examples.text: По легенде, рыбу запекали на мечах.
examples.trans: According to legend, fish was baked on swords.

examples.text: Крестоносцы готовили рыбу прямо на мечах.
examples.trans: The Crusaders prepared fish right on their swords.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: кого + instrumental: назвать меня плохим словом
Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'звать').

examples.trans: You called me a bad word.
What will you name your son?

examples.text: Ты назвал меня плохим словом. Меня, начальника!
examples.trans: You called me a bad word. Me, your boss!

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
end-stressed in all oblique forms: ножа, ножом

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!
There is a sharp knife on the table.

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.
I will explain everything to you right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Takes the instrumental.

examples.trans: I'm standing in front of you.
There's a car in front of the house.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: In 'по поводу' + genitive.
+ dative.
'по телефону'.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Позвольте = allow me (polite).

examples.trans: Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.

examples.text: Прошу, присаживайтесь. Позвольте, я сделаю удобнее.
examples.trans: Please, have a seat. Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.

meanings.note: On foot.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is true poetry of haute cuisine.
The guest called the dish pure poetry.

examples.trans: Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

meanings.note: Прямо так = just like that.

examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

examples.text: Шеф хранит свой тайный рецепт супа.

examples.trans: Really? This is my old signature recipe.

meanings.note: Animal or food.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать').

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Used as imperative exhortation.
Comparison.
без спроса / без спросу = without asking
спрос и предложение = supply and demand

examples.trans: Don't take other people's things without asking.
There is high demand for these flats.

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса, да?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking, yes?

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: belonging to ancient times or heritage

examples.text: Наша старинная стена теперь полностью спасена.
examples.trans: Our ancient wall is now completely saved.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I

examples.text: И огурцы тоже можно, можно всё, что хотите! Получаются уникальные вкусы.
examples.trans: And cucumbers are fine too, anything you want! You get unique flavours.

examples.text: Главное сохранить этот уникальный древний монастырь.
examples.trans: The main thing is to preserve this unique ancient monastery.

Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: instrumental чем-то: чем-то помочь = help with something

examples.text: Так может быть, тебе надо чем-то помочь?
examples.trans: So maybe you need help with something?

meanings.note: Informal. Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!
